holidays.name: Mean Girls Day
holidays.description: Fans of the 2004 cult-classic comedy wear pink, trade quotes like "That's so fetch," and rewatch the movie. It's a day for gossip-free (mostly) nostalgia and Burn Book jokes.
holidays.origin: The date comes from a scene in Mean Girls. Aaron Samuels tells Cady Heron the date, and she answers with a line about the day. Fans began celebrating each year on October 3, and the movie's cast and studio now join in online.
holidays.funFact: The movie's script was inspired by Rosalind Wiseman's parenting book about teenage cliques, 'Queen Bees and Wannabes.'

holidays.name: National Caramel Custard Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the silky, wobbly dessert with a glossy caramel topping. Grab a spoon and flip a flan, crème caramel or caramel custard onto a plate in one dramatic move.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It honors a dessert whose roots go back to Europe, where cooks have long used eggs to set sweet custards.
holidays.funFact: Ancient Romans experimented with using eggs to bind dishes, but custard as we know it didn't appear until the Middle Ages.

holidays.name: National Boyfriend Day
holidays.description: A social media-fueled holiday for appreciating your boyfriend with notes, snacks, small gifts or a nice date. It's meant to be a sweet, low-pressure way to say thanks.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance that grew popular in the 2010s, mostly through social media posts. It's often paired with National Girlfriend Day in August.
holidays.funFact: Many people mark the day by posting throwback photos with their partner, which has helped it trend online every year.
